title: The draft genome sequence of a desert tree Populus pruinosa
author: Unknown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ii5ccg6
materials: we annotated tandem repeats using the software Tandem Repeat Finder (TRF v4.07b) trf Ppr_genome.fa 2 7 7 80 10 50 2000 -d -h TRF v4.07b

we use the software TransDecoder v2.1.0 to identify candidate coding regions within the transcript sequences we filtered at step 12. TransDecoder v2.1.0 linux https://github.com/TransDecoder/TransDecoder/releases TransDecoder.LongOrfs -t cd-hit_out.fa;TransDecoder.Predict -t cd-hit_out.fa TransDecoder v4.6.1 TransDecoder.LongOrfs -t cd-hit_out.fa; TransDecoder.Predict -t cd-hit_out.fa TransDecoder v4.6.1

steps.title: Filter Raw Sequences
steps.instruction: Perform quality control and filtering on raw input sequences using a series of tools.

substeps.instruction: Filter raw sequences using Lighter v1.0.7: `lighter -r *.1.filter.fq.gz -r *.2.filter.fq.gz -k 17 590000000 alpha -t 10 -trim`
Filter sequences using the custom script `01.QualityControlAndMergeReads.pl`
Remove duplicates using Fastuniq v1.1: `fastuniq -i reads_list.txt -t q -o *.1.filter.fq -p *.2.filter.fq`

steps.title: Assemble Genome
steps.instruction: Assemble the genome and close gaps using Platanus v1.2.1.

substeps.instruction: Run assembly: `platanus assemble -f xx.1.fq xx.2.fq ... -t 50 -m 290 -o Ppr`

Generate scaffolds: `platanus scaffold -o Ppr -c Ppr_contig.fa -b Ppr_contigBubble.fa -t 64 -IP1 158bp.1.fq 158bp.2.fq -IP2 483bp.1.fq 483bp.2.fq -IP3 780bp.1.fq 780bp.2.fq -OP4 2k.1.fq 2k.2.fq -OP5 5k.1.fq 5k.2.fq -OP6 ...`

Close gaps: `platanus gap_close -c Ppr_scaffold.fa -o platanus_gapclose -t 64 -IP1 158bp.1.fq 158bp.2.fq -IP2 483bp.1.fq 483bp.2.fq -IP3 780bp.1.fq 780bp.2.fq -OP4 2k.1.fq 2k.2.fq -OP5 5k.1.fq 5k.2.fq -OP6 ...`

steps.title: Estimate Genome Size
steps.instruction: Estimate the genome size using k-mer analysis with SOAP v2.2 (SOAPec).

steps.title: Further Close Genome Gaps
steps.instruction: Use GapCloser v1.02/1.12 to further close gaps in the assembly.

substeps.instruction: Run GapCloser: `BGI GapCloser -a scaffold.fa -b soapGapClose.config -o Ppr_GapCloser.fa -t 64 -l 100`

steps.title: Evaluate Assembly Completeness and Correctness
steps.instruction: Assess the quality of the genome assembly using BUSCO and FRC.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate completeness of the assembly using BUSCO v1.22.
Evaluate the trade-off between contiguity and correctness using FRC v1.3.0: `FRC --genome-size 590000000 --pe-sam 483bp.bam --mp-sam 2000bp.bam --pe-max-insert 500 --mp-max-insert 2000 --out frcurve`

steps.title: Perform Variant Calling
steps.instruction: Map clean reads and call variants using BWA and GATK.

substeps.instruction: Map paired-end libraries using BWA v0.7.12: `bwa mem -t 12 -R '@RG ID: ...'`
Perform variant calling using GATK v3.5, including `RealignerTargetCreator` and `IndelRealigner` with `-Xmx10g` memory settings.

steps.title: Identify and Mask Repeats
steps.instruction: Identify repeats at DNA and protein levels and build a de novo library.

substeps.instruction: Run RepeatMasker v4.0.6: `RepeatMasker -nolow -no_is -norna -parallel 1 -species`
Run RepeatProteinMask v4.0.6: `RepeatProteinMask -engine abblast -noLowSimple -pvalue 0.0001 Ppr_genome.fa`
Build de novo library using RepeatModeler v1.0.8: `BuildDatabase -name ppr Ppr_genome.fa` followed by `RepeatModeler -pa 30 -database ppr`
Mask genome using the generated library: `RepeatMasker -lib RM*/consensi.fa.classified -pa 30 Ppr_genome.fa`

steps.title: Predict Genes
steps.instruction: Predict genes using homology-based, de novo, and transcriptome-based approaches.

substeps.instruction: Homology-based: Align protein sequences from P. euphratica, P. trichocarpa, Ricinus communis, Arabidopsis thaliana, Carica papaya, and Eucalyptus grandis using BLAST, process with BLAST2GENE v17, and predict genes with GeneWise v2.4.1.
De novo: Predict genes in repeat-masked sequences using Augustus v3.2.1 and GenScan.
Transcriptome-based: Assemble RNA-seq reads using Trinity v2.1.1, reduce redundancy (>95% similarity) using CD-Hit v4.6.1, align transcripts to the genome, and assemble using PASA v2.0.2.

steps.title: Integrate Gene Sets
steps.instruction: Obtain a consensus gene set by integrating predictions from the homology, de novo, and transcriptome methods using EVM v1.1.1.

steps.title: Analyze Gene Expression
steps.instruction: Align transcriptome reads from three tissues to the genome using TopHat v2.1.1 and compute expression using Cufflinks v2.2.1.

steps.title: Perform Comparative Genomics
steps.instruction: Analyze synteny and genome alignment between P. pruinosa and P. euphratica.

substeps.instruction: Determine syntenic blocks using MCScanX (default parameters, minimum 5 genes for synteny).

Perform whole-genome alignment using LAST v802: `lastdb -uNEAR -cR11 ref_db ref.fa`, `lastal -P48 -m100 -E 0.05 ref_db Ppr_genome.fa | last-split > query2db.maf`, and `maf-swap query2db.maf | last-split > query2db.maf.sing.maf`

steps.title: Analyze Gene Families and Phylogeny
steps.instruction: Cluster gene families and construct a phylogenetic tree.

substeps.instruction: Cluster protein-coding genes of P. pruinosa and 10 other species (P. euphratica, P. trichocarpa, Salix suchowensis, Ricinus communis, A. thaliana, C. papaya, F. vesca, C. sativus, E. grandis, V. vinifera) using OrthoMCL v3.1/v2.0.9.
Align single-copy gene families with MUSCLE v3.8.31, trim with Gblocks v0.91b, and construct a phylogenetic tree using RAxML v8.2.8 (model GTRGAMMA, -T 30).

steps.title: Estimate Divergence and Evolution
steps.instruction: Analyze divergence times and gene family evolution.

substeps.instruction: Estimate divergence time using MCMCTree (PAML v4.9) with fossil calibrations: A. thaliana/C. papaya (54-90 Mya), A. thaliana/R. communis (95-109 Mya), and V. vinifera/A. thaliana (106-119 Mya).
Examine gene family evolution using CAFÉ v3.1.

steps.title: Functional Annotation
steps.instruction: Map protein sequences of the final gene set to databases including SwissProt, TrEMBL, KEGG, and InterPro to identify functions and motifs.
